text: Track 1.1 Hi everyone, thanks for coming. Today I'm going to talk about working at an animal shelter. I want to start by saying that animal shelters are always looking for people to work for them. There are so many animals to look after. For example, in the summer of 2018, the RSPCA, that the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, got around 20,000 calls about abandoned animals, animals that are left because people don't want them. That's one every six minutes. Anyway, let me talk about the advantages of working at a shelter. By the way, there are more advantages than disadvantages. First of all, you know that you are doing a good thing, and you're making sure the animals get all the care they need. It's a fantastic feeling to see an animal find a home, even though it is a lot of hard work to get an animal ready in the first place, especially those that have survived in difficult places. Luckily, not all animals that come to us have suffered abuse. On the contrary, their owners loved and cared for them, but had to give them up because they were no longer able to look after them. It's very sad, but we're working very hard to find them good homes. Furthermore, working at a shelter is good for your health too. It's a fact that spending time with animals helps you feel less stressed. Some universities in the UK actually use animals during exams to help students with stress. And a number of airlines let passengers travel with their pets to help with the anxiety of flying. Connecting with animals has a positive effect on your mood, helps you to be more relaxed and happier. Another point is that you get to know the animals over a long period of time, which is important for people who want to take an animal home. You can tell them about the animal's character and any training it needs. Finally, you see them go to a good home. You have done all you can to help. You know they are going to a place where they will be safe and looked after. However, working at a shelter has some disadvantages too. Knowing about the abuse the animal suffered and the conditions they lived in before can make you feel unhappy. It can also be very difficult to see an animal leave the shelter, especially one that has become your friend. In most cases, it's the last time you will see these animals. Another disadvantage is more to do with the number of animals that are here. This is certainly a problem in the shelter where I work. We receive more animals than we can handle and we work hard to make more space for them all the time. Crowded places make animals anxious and disease can also be an issue. That's why we need more people. To sum up, working at an animal shelter has both pros and cons, but it's a very rewarding job. It doesn't only benefit your welfare, it benefits the welfare of all the animals in the shelter too.
